notes.content:
**Executive summary:** In the 18th century **Bengal was the richest Indian province** — fertile and prosperous, it drew Dutch, French and English traders. Two battles — **Plassey (1757)** and **Buxar (1764)** — made the British masters of Bengal, followed by the **Dual Government (1765–72)**.

**Farman of 1717:** Mughal emperor **Farrukhsiyar** granted the EEIC **duty-free trade in Bengal** and the right to issue **dastaks** (passes) → British settlement became the richest; officials amassed wealth.
• Under Nawab **Alivardi Khan**, the British fortified their factories.
• His grandson **Siraj-ud-Daulah** ordered the British to **pay taxes** — they refused → conflict.

**Chapter map:** Farman → Plassey → Mir Jafar → Mir Qasim → Buxar → Treaty of Allahabad → Dual Government → Famine 1770 → Warren Hastings.

fiveW.who: Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah vs the British (Robert Clive), with Mir Jafar
fiveW.what: Build-up to the Battle of Plassey
fiveW.why: Misuse of trade privileges, illegal fortification, British wish for a puppet Nawab
fiveW.how: Nawab captured Calcutta; Clive recaptured it; conspiracy with Mir Jafar

notes.content:
• **Misuse of dastaks** and refusal to pay taxes.
• **Fortifications:** expecting war with the French (at **Chandernagore**), the British fortified **Calcutta without permission**. The Nawab ordered both to pull down fortifications — the **French agreed, the British refused**.
• **Capture of Calcutta (1756):** Siraj seized **Fort William**; **Clive recaptured** Calcutta.
• **Treaty of Alinagar:** Nawab **restored trading rights and Calcutta** and allowed fortification.
• British still wanted a **puppet ruler**; with **Mir Jafar** (the Nawab's commander) they made **unreasonable demands** → war inevitable.

notes.subtopic: 3. Battle of Plassey — Battle, Results, Importance

fiveW.who: Robert Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah; traitors Mir Jafar and Jagat Seth
fiveW.what: British victory; Mir Jafar made Nawab
fiveW.why: British wanted control of Bengal's wealth
fiveW.how: Conspiracy — Mir Jafar's large force did not fight; the Nawab fled after Mir Madan's death

notes.content:
**The battle (June 1757):** Siraj had about **50,000** men. **Mir Jafar's** large section **did not fight**; after commander **Mir Madan** died, the Nawab left the field; the army was defeated. Siraj was captured and killed; **Mir Jafar became a puppet Nawab**.
• **Jagat Seth** — rich Marwari **banker** of Murshidabad — conspired with Mir Jafar and Clive.

**Results:** undisputed right to trade in **Bengal, Bihar, Orissa**; **zamindari of the 24 Parganas**; huge payment from Mir Jafar.

**Importance — a turning point**
• Paved the way for **British rule in India**.
• EEIC changed from a **trading company into a political power**.
• Bengal's **wealth** financed the **Third Carnatic War** and further conquests.

**Mir Jafar — 'Nawab only in name'**: responsibilities but **no power**; the Company plundered Bengal and made it pay for the **Bombay and Madras Presidencies**. He sought help from the **Dutch**, but the British defeated them at **Chinsurah**. The British **deposed** him.

**Mir Qasim** (Mir Jafar's **son-in-law**) — ambitious and able
• Gave the British zamindari of **Burdwan, Midnapore, Chittagong**.
• Moved capital from **Murshidabad to Monghyr**, away from British control.
• Hired **French officers** to train a modern army.
• **Abolished all duties on internal trade** for Indians too → ended British advantage → wars.

fiveW.who: Mir Qasim + Shuja-ud-Daulah (Awadh) + Shah Alam II (Mughal) vs the British
fiveW.why: Mir Qasim wanted to recover Bengal
fiveW.how: Three-power alliance lost to the British army

notes.content:
• Mir Qasim allied with **Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh)** and **Shah Alam II (Mughal emperor)**.
• The combined forces were **completely defeated**.

**Results**
• Beginning of **British colonial oppression** in Bengal; British became **absolute masters of Bengal**.
• **Political control over Awadh**.
• **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** — **Shah Alam II and Robert Clive** — British got the **diwani** (right to collect revenue) of **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa**.
• **Awadh** became a **buffer state** between British Bengal and the Marathas; British would defend Awadh, but the Nawab paid for British troops.

**Plassey vs Buxar:** Plassey was won by **conspiracy**; Buxar by **military strength** against three Indian powers — Buxar confirmed British supremacy.

fiveW.who: Robert Clive's system — the Company and the Nawab
fiveW.what: Two parallel governments: British held revenue and army, the Nawab ran administration
fiveW.why: Company wanted power and wealth without responsibility
fiveW.how: British collected revenue; Nawab disbanded his army and got a small allowance

notes.content:
| British (Company) | Nawab |
|---|---|
| **Power without responsibility** | **Responsibility without power** |
| Complete **military power** | Had to **disband most of his army** |
| **Collected revenue** (diwani), used it as they wished | Got a **small amount** to run civil administration |
| | Looked after administration, law and order |

**Effects**
• **Corruption** of tax officials grew.
• **Misery of peasants** increased.
• **Great Famine of 1770** — **more than one-third** of Bengal's population died; the British cared only for wealth.

**End (1772):** administration and economy collapsed → Company took **direct control** → **Warren Hastings** Governor of Bengal → by the **Regulating Act of 1773**, **first Governor-General**; credited with an **organised system of government** in Bengal.

questions.question: Which was the richest Indian province in the 18th century? Who was Jagat Seth?
questions.answer:
• Bengal.
  • Jagat Seth — a rich Marwari banker of Murshidabad, called 'the greatest banker in the known world' by the EEIC historian Robert Orme; he conspired with Mir Jafar and Clive against Siraj-ud-Daulah.

questions.question: What were the terms of the Treaty of Alinagar?
questions.answer: Signed between the British and Siraj-ud-Daulah after Clive recaptured Calcutta: the Nawab restored the British trading rights and the city of Calcutta, and allowed them to fortify Calcutta.

questions.question: What were the causes of the Battle of Plassey?
questions.answer:
• Misuse of trade privileges (dastaks) and refusal to pay taxes to Siraj-ud-Daulah.
  • Illegal fortification of Calcutta; British refused to pull it down (the French agreed).
  • Siraj captured Calcutta (1756); Clive recaptured it → Treaty of Alinagar.
  • British wanted a puppet Nawab; they conspired with Mir Jafar and made unreasonable demands.

questions.question: Why is the Battle of Plassey considered a turning point in Indian history?
questions.answer:
• It paved the way for British rule in India.
  • The Nawab became a puppet; the EEIC changed from a trading company into a political power.
  • Bengal's vast resources passed to the British and financed the Third Carnatic War and later conquests.
  • The Company got undisputed trade rights in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa and the 24 Parganas.
questions.topperTip: 'Trader to ruler' is the key phrase for Plassey.

questions.question: 'Mir Jafar was a Nawab only in name.' Do you support the statement?
questions.answer:
Yes.

  • He was placed on the throne by the British as a puppet.
  • He had responsibilities but no power; the Company plundered Bengal and made it pay for Bombay and Madras.
  • When he sought Dutch help, the British defeated the Dutch at Chinsurah and deposed him.

questions.question: Describe the reforms of Mir Qasim. Why did they anger the British?
questions.answer:
• Shifted the capital from Murshidabad to Monghyr, away from British control.
  • Hired French officers to train a modern, well-equipped army.
  • Reorganised the chaotic administration.
  • Abolished all duties on internal trade for Indians too — this ended the British monopoly from duty-free trade and enraged them, leading to war.

questions.question: (Picture) Nawab who was the son-in-law of an earlier Nawab — identify him, his battle and his role.
questions.answer:
• (a) Mir Qasim.
  • (b) Battle of Buxar (1764).
  • (c) He formed an alliance with Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II to recover Bengal and led the combined forces against the British.

questions.question: What were the results of the Battle of Buxar? How did it affect common people?
questions.answer:
• British became absolute masters of Bengal; gained political control over Awadh.
  • Treaty of Allahabad (1765) — diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa.
  • Awadh became a buffer state.
  • Common people: it began colonial oppression — heavy revenue demands, corrupt collectors, and finally the famine of 1770.

questions.question: When and between whom was the Treaty of Allahabad signed? What did the British gain?
questions.answer: In 1765, between the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II and Robert Clive. The British got the diwani — the right to collect revenue — of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

questions.question: What was the Dual Government? State its effects.
questions.answer:
• System set up by Robert Clive in 1765 — two parallel governments in Bengal.
  • British: all military power and revenue — power without responsibility.
  • Nawab: administration and law and order with a small allowance, army disbanded — responsibility without power.
  • Effects: corruption of tax collectors; misery of peasants; Great Famine of 1770 — over one-third of people died.
questions.topperTip: Draw the British vs Nawab two-column table — quick and scoring.

questions.question: Why did the Dual Government collapse? Who introduced an organised system of government in Bengal?
questions.answer:
• Its defects became visible to the British Parliament; Bengal's administration and economy collapsed after the famine of 1770.
  • In 1772 the Company took direct control and appointed Warren Hastings, who became first Governor-General under the Regulating Act (1773).
  • Hastings is credited with an organised system of government in Bengal.
